# tsk

> tsk is a terminal task board for you and your agents: one shared queue, a TUI for you, a CLI for them.

The human works the board in a TUI; agents read and write the same tasks with the `tsk` CLI. It ships as the `herdr-tsk` plugin for Herdr and also runs standalone in any terminal.

## Install

- macOS and Linux: `curl -fsSL https://gettsk.sh/install.sh | sh`, or `brew install smarzban/tap/tsk`.
- Windows 10/11, ARM64 or x86-64: `irm https://www.gettsk.sh/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell.
- `tsk setup herdr` adds the board to Herdr, `tsk setup` installs the agent skill, and `tsk update` upgrades. Details: https://gettsk.sh/docs/install.md

## Concepts

- Status: `open` (inbox), `ready` (picked), `started`, `blocked`, `review`, `done`. The human owns status; checking every step never completes a task.
- Desk and project: a project is a Git repository root, named by its folder. The desk holds tasks with no project.
- Thread: a label that groups related work, within a project or across several.
- Task number: `T12`, `12`, and the task's UUID address the same task.
- Notice: `N` rows on the desk (starter tasks, What's new) are for the human only. `tsk list` never shows them.
- Agent profile: an `[agent.<name>]` table in `config.toml` holding the command that launches an agent.
- Assignee: an agent profile, the human (`you`), or a named person. Only an agent assignee dispatches.
- Dispatch: in Herdr, starting a project task assigned to an agent launches it in a new Git worktree and Herdr workspace, from the task's base branch.
- Block: a task waiting on an answer, with why, what it needs, and options to choose from. Replies answer it; unblocking sends them to the running dispatched agent. `tsk edit T12 --on <who>` changes who an open block or review waits on.
- Review: work handed back with what was done and checks to verify. The human marks the checks, then approves or sends it back with feedback.
- After: a task waits until the tasks it runs after are done. The last done starts it if it is ready.
- Paper trail: who changed what on a task, newest first.

## For agents

- Run `tsk guide` first: it prints the workflow and the rules. `tsk help <command>` is the syntax reference.
- Read with `tsk list --json`. `tsk list T12 --json` returns one task in full: notes, steps, block, review, dispatch, and `activity`.
- Write with `tsk add`, `tsk edit`, and `tsk steps`. Read the exit code before any retry; `tsk dispatch`, `tsk edit --append-notes`, and some `tsk steps` commands are not idempotent.
- When your work is finished, hand it back: `tsk status T12 review --done "…" --check "…"`. Set `done` only when the user says so.
- When you need the human: `tsk status T12 blocked --why "…" --option "…"`, then stop. `tsk reply T12 "…"` answers a block or adds review feedback.
- `tsk dispatch T12` launches an assigned project task's agent in Herdr. `tsk clean T12` removes its worktree and merged branch; never clean the worktree you run in.
- Inside a dispatched agent, `TSK_AGENT` names the profile as the author of each change.
- Guide: https://gettsk.sh/docs/agents.md
